title: Severe Thermal, Chemical, and Electrical Burns
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid Guidelines 2020; American Burn Association (ABA) Initial Burn Assessment Guidelines

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately for burns covering large areas, burns to face, hands, joints, or genitals, or chemical/electrical burns
Ensure your own safety: isolate electrical power source, extinguish flames, or move away from hot liquids or chemical fumes
Cool the burn immediately under clean, running, cool or lukewarm tap water for at least 20 minutes (or until ambulance arrives)
Gently remove jewelry, watches, belts, and loose non-adherent clothing before swelling begins
Cover the cooled burn loosely with clean, non-adherent sterile dressing or clear plastic cling film laid flat
Keep the rest of the patient's body warm with dry blankets to prevent systemic hypothermia

do_not: Do not apply ice, ice water, or freezing compresses to burned skin (causes further tissue damage)
Do not peel off clothing that is stuck or melted into the burn wound
Do not break or puncture any burn blisters
Do not apply butter, oil, toothpaste, flour, turmeric, or unproven home remedies to burned skin
